Project assessment · 7 September 2026

The Newcastle twin, at thirty families and none inside the band

A city digital twin of Newcastle, New South Wales — twelve modes, each physically simulated on the real roads and timetables and scored against its real-life ridership. Twenty-eight days old, 465 commits, 480 declared values, 374 machine hours. It is the only project of forty-six surveyed worldwide aiming at a per-mode fit for every mode it simulates, and it is not yet on that rung: at this commit no mode is inside ten percent, and no arm in the project's history has been allowed past iteration 100 of a 250-iteration convergence requirement.

The verdict, in one paragraph

This is an unusually well-built research instrument that has not yet been allowed to take its measurement. The engineering discipline is real and checkable: 480 controllable values declared with units and provenance, hard-coding gated at zero in CI, a manifest of 512 hashed files, a record of 152 append-only sections, and a session gate of eighteen checks that presently fails on one — a board that is a single run behind. In seven days the iteration has been decomposed from inside the JVM and cut from 639 s to 205.5 s, with this project's own code falling from 56.2% of an iteration to 0.4%. What has not moved is the thing the project exists to do. No mode is inside ten percent, eight of twelve are past the twenty-percent stop bar, and requirement 8 — convergence within 250 iterations — has never been tested: across 158 runs and 28 days the deepest reading is iteration 100. Thirty comparability families have been opened and closed, 38% of all machine time bought no citable reading, and seventeen open issues are queued behind one arm nobody has launched. The instrument is now cheap enough to run — 13.5 to 18 hours by measurement — and the launcher is quoting 26.3 hours because it prices the arm on a run that predates its own repair. The single most valuable thing this project could do next is buy one uninterrupted arm and let it finish.

The measurement the project exists to make

Twelve modes, none inside ten percent

The board's generated scoreboard reads from aborted_20260907T150816_300it_25pct at iteration 20 — an arm of family F30-an-escort-is-priced-as-an-escort that the operator stopped on cost at iteration 23. It is not a result. Only a run whose _run.json says ran_to_last_iteration is one, and no arm since family F4 (21 August) has reached its declared horizon. A stopped arm's reading is citable at its reached_iteration and nowhere past it, which is what the figures below are.

Method

What was read, by whom, and how it was rated

The passes

7 · The factorsthe library's literature half reused; all 72 statuses re-read at HEAD by grep21 of 40 calls; three literature halves closed; the status counts

The rating rubric

scoremeaning
5correct, clear and guarded by a check that would catch a regression
4sound, with a named weakness that is documented and bounded
3works, but a reader must hold something in their head that the code does not say
2a defect is reachable by ordinary use, or a rule is broken silently
1wrong in a way that would change a result, or unguarded where the project's own constraints demand a guard

What this report is not

It changed nothing in the model, the data, the registry, the board, the brief, a position page or the record. It launched no run, recompiled nothing and opened no issue. The only files it wrote are itself, its index row, and the two reference-library files under docs/reports/reference/. It never read DECISIONS.md, SESSION_LOG.md or CONFIG_REFERENCE.md whole, and never read a matsim.log whole.

Verification

Ten cited file:lines were re-read directly at f40d332 and the reference library's reused rows were verified by inspection — each carries at least one source URL and a last_verified date inside its horizon. Rows reused from the library are marked reused in the survey table so a reader can see exactly what was checked this pass and what was inherited.

Phase 4 · the record, read end to end

Twenty-eight days, thirty families, one completed arm era

The repository's root commit is dated 10 August 2026. Everything below is dated by an artefact — a merge commit, a run directory, a DECISIONS.md section — and a milestone with no artefact date is listed as undated rather than placed on the line.

stage complete stage in progress comparability family opened run or gate pull request merged record sections

What happened when

  1. 10 August - the repository opens with one commit called 'proposal' and, within nine hours, three merged pull requests: P1's 182-file hashed data package, P2's 157,678-link MATSim network with all 15 GTFS feeds mapped, and P3's tour-based demand. None of it had been run, and all three PRs say so.
  2. 11 August - the first attempt to execute MATSim refuses to load all thirty assembled run-input sets. PR #4 fixes three defects, measures the first cost curve (9.8 / 29.9 / ~64 s an iteration) and records that thirteen of the sixty-seven calibration targets can identify nothing.
  3. 15-16 August - PR #38's rebuild: a typed-in OSM harvest box had clipped 87 core SA1s out of the road network. Core SA1s without a road node fall 99 to 4, the config is emitted from 297 declared registry fields, and family F1 produces the project's first completed 1000-iteration arm.
  4. 18-21 August - ride pairing is built and immediately measured starved (0.104 % of ride trips share an OD with a household car trip); escort binding and census age structure repair the demand; every person-transport mode becomes physical (F3); the walk wedge is found and repaired (F4) - the last family to date whose arms ran to their declared horizon.
  5. 20-21 August - process hardens after five of six stacked pull requests never reach main: PRs target main only, direct commits to main are banned, and the session's one PR opens at /handoff. The sixth and last direct commit lands seventeen minutes before the rule merges; there has not been one since.
  6. 24-25 August - SUMO is descoped by recorded decision, the signals run stack is pinned by sha256, and the all-modes batch is built inert with byte-identical run inputs, then activated as family F6. The first gate stop follows the same day, and check_doc_currency.py pins every live-state number in the front door to its artefact.
  7. 27-29 August - the gate loop starts firing on the twenty-percent bar. PR #95 fixes three yardsticks that had been wrong at every iteration - one counted another city's light rail stop - and corrects four of its own session's conclusions in the same body.
  8. 30 August - the busiest day of the project: 87 commits, six comparability families (F15-F20), 31 record sections, a demand rebuilt twice, and the document restructure into GOAL.md, a one-page generated board and thirteen position pages, so a session reads 600 lines instead of a 13,000-line record.
  9. 31 August - 2 September - public transport is priced at the published Opal fare, then bike stress, parking search and income-scaled money sensitivity enter the model. Bus comes inside its band at the F22 gate, the first of the twelve modes ever to; the results store makes the run lifecycle automatic.
  10. 3-6 September - the first whole-repository assessment lodges 26 issues and the next PR closes fourteen without a run; destination choice is constrained at both ends; F25 falsifies the demand-side cause for ride; a declared driver must own a car (F26); and a global qsim wait strands every non-chain mode (F27), citable for nothing.
  11. 7 September, morning - at the F28 gate car reads +6.6 %, inside the band at a gate for the first time, with ride still -42.8 % and seven modes past the bar. Two more assessments land in six hours: PR #152 closes 29 of 34 defects (the 67/143 holdout had been informing the count targets; heavy share 0.0652 -> 0.1120) and PR #153 rules on the five that block a launch, opening F30 on a seeded draw that had been following HashMap order.
  12. 7 September, afternoon - F30's first arm is launched, refused once by a toolchain gate that had been green on a missing run stack, then run and stopped at iteration 23 for costing 45 % more than its approval. PR #156 finds out why: half a plain iteration's CPU was this project's own router re-deriving per link what never changes. Tables cut it 310 -> 205.5 s, a declared value is found to have reached nothing since it existed (#154), and the two-minute iteration the directive asked for is still not reached.

Churn — what changes most

Four of the top six files a commit touches are documents, and three of the top seven are generated output committed by the reproducibility rule. That is correct by design, and it means a typical pull-request diff is dominated by files no human reads.

Build layer

Depth of read

13 of 36 files opened directly (~2,600 of 16,616 lines), the rest verified by targeted grep at every prior-report citation. Read substantially: src/build/build_manifest.py (whole, 471), src/build/det_io.py (whole, 75), src/build/build_matsim_run_inputs.py (~700 of 1777: head, FLEET_CAPACITY, CAR_COMPANION_MODES, patch_network, stamp_gradients, stamp_bike_stress, PT_SUBMODE_ASC, main), src/build/build_matsim_plans.py (~450 of 1537: module head, attrs(), write_day opening 170 lines), src/build/build_activity_chains.py (~260 of 3288: constant block, load_network_factors, solve_day_rates, legs_per_tour), src/build/build_population.py (~130 of 422: the SA1 draw loop), src/build/shape_tools.py (~130 of 397), src/build/build_matsim_network.py (~110 of 615: JAVA_XMX, java(), write_mapper_config, map_feed, main CLI), src/build/measure_network_factors.py (~40), src/build/build_gtfs_extras.py (~50 of 209), cities/newcastle/build/build_corridor_layers.py (~50 of 400), cities/newcastle/build/build_charging_dwell_offsets.py (~20), cities/newcastle/build/build_matsim_signals.py (~20), cities/newcastle/build/build_landuse_parking.py (~50 of 494), cities/newcastle/build/build_mode_targets.py (60 of 810), cities/newcastle/build/build_validation_targets.py (~40 of 430 plus a full grep of its split logic). BLIND SPOT, named: build_scenario_schedules.py (824), build_corridor_road_attributes.py (698), build_level_crossings.py (512), build_licence_rates.py (242), build_params.py (288), measure_osm_defaults.py (218), build_scenario_configs.py (201), build_era1_reconstruction.py (179), attach_speed_zones.py (150), build_zone_attractions.py (138), attach_gradient.py (135), build_era_feeds.py (131), build_external_interaction.py (119), gtfs_tools.py (113), normalise_eol.py (87), map_sa1_to_lga.py (71), build_data_dictionary.py (69), osm_parse.py (61), hts_purpose.py (28) went unread. SEVEN of those carry code_metrics rows: build_scenario_schedules.py main (174 lines, complexity 17), build_corridor_road_attributes.py build (108 lines, complexity 29), build_level_crossings.py main (234 lines, complexity 46), build_landuse_parking.py build_poi (nesting 10) and build_frontages (101 lines, nesting 6, read), build_gtfs_extras.py main (complexity 49, partly read), build_data_dictionary.py (the repository's ONE dead module, bare except at :39), gtfs_tools.py (bare except at :38). Their rows are reported below from the metrics, not from a read, and that is stated on each.

The build layer is a one-way pipeline of standalone scripts, each with a module docstring that states what it consumes, what it emits and which DECISIONS section justifies its choices; every one resolves paths through src/city.py and values through src/registry, and the framework half (src/build) is genuinely city-free apart from three residues named below. The split between src/build (portable construction) and cities/newcastle/build (this city's intervention, corridor, statistical geography and survey vocabulary) is real and mostly respected. Determinism is taken seriously at the level of the seeded generator, sorted iteration and the det_io gzip/zip writers, and the one class of prior defect there - the stdlib gzip header - is now closed at both sites. The layer's weakness is scale and inspectability: three files carry 6,600 of its 16,600 lines, write_day is 742 lines at cyclomatic complexity 151 and nesting 10, and the migration of decided values into the registry stopped at the ALL-CAPS module-level constant. Everything below that line - a dict(...) constant, a two-number sweep tuple, a lower-case number inside a function body - is invisible to both check_hardcoding.py and extract_legacy_constants.py, and that is where most of the model's remaining assumptions live. The network assembly is also I/O-shaped by accretion: the run network is read, regex-rewritten and written back five times per scenario.

defectcities/newcastle/build/build_corridor_layers.py:122DWELL_DEFAULTS = dict(dwell_charging_s=20.0, dwell_charging_sweep=(10.0,35.0), ...) is a live second copy of A.lightrail.dwell_charging_s, which the registry declares value:null / status:unobtained and refuses to pin - and check_legacy_drift.py:39-40 asserts in prose that the constant is gone.A sweep moves A.lightrail.dwell_charging_s to 35 s through the scenario overlay to test the corridor's worst case. defectsrc/build/build_manifest.py:262_script_path resolves a producing-script token against the CURRENT WORKING DIRECTORY (os.path.exists(token), then cities/<city>/token), so a derived file's whole source/source_url/retrieved lineage is a function of where the manifest was built from.The manifest is regenerated from cities/newcastle/ rather than the repo root. os.path.exists('src/build/build_population.py') is false, the cities/<city>/ fallback also misses, _script_inputs returns an empty set, raw_ancestors finds nothing, and derived_provenance writes an EMPTY source, source_url and retrieved for every derived row. check_manifest.py refuses only a blank licence, so the regenerated manifest passes CI with the provenance of the processed half silently deleted.open
defectsrc/build/build_manifest.py:348record_for gives a raw file with no provenance record of its own the LEXICOGRAPHICALLY FIRST sibling record in its directory that carries a `retrieved` date, so an undated file inherits a neighbour's source, url and retrieval date as though they were its own.A new download is unpacked into data/raw/opal/ beside the existing Opal records but its own provenance_*.json is not written yet. The manifest run attributes it to whichever sibling sorts first by path, and the row states a source URL and a retrieval date that describe a different acquisition. No check compares a row's source against the file's actual origin, so an unsourced file is published as a sourced one - the one failure class CLAUDE.md says the project cannot absorb.open
defectsrc/build/build_matsim_plans.py:397A dead household_vehicles branch: p is read with an explicit usecols list at :390-393 that does not include household_vehicles, so `if 'household_vehicles' in p.columns` at :398 can never be true and the roster is always re-read from B1_households.csv.Not a wrong number today, but the branch is a trap: anyone adding household_vehicles to the usecols list (an obvious optimisation) silently switches the roster source from B1_households.csv to a groupby-max over the person table, which for a household whose members carry differing values would change ride availability - the attribute RidePairingEngine and sample_population both key on - with no test and no error.open
risksrc/build/build_population.py:307Income (p_inc, :310) and occupation (p_occ, :307) are drawn independently of age, sex and employment status, and household vehicles (:297, :324) independently of household size, composition and income, although the census publishes every one of those joint tables and they are already under data/processed/census/.C.income.representation = person_marginal_utility_of_money makes each person's income scale their marginal utility of money. Because income is drawn from the SA1 total rather than conditioned on employment, a synthetic 17-year-old not in the labour force can draw the top income band and a full-time professional the bottom one; the model then prices their time backwards, and the car/PT trade-off is wrong for exactly the segments a light-rail counterfactual turns on. Same mechanism for car-less hoopen
risksrc/build/build_population.py:282residence_marginals returning None makes the SA1 loop `continue` silently, with no counter and no line in the build report; the same for `asd.sum() <= 0` at :288 and `pop <= 0` at :277/:281.A census table's column names change in a re-download. residence_marginals raises KeyError internally, returns None for every SA1, and build_population writes a population file with far fewer persons and no error at all. Nothing in the report says how many zones were dropped, so the shortfall reads as a smaller city rather than a broken read.open
risksrc/build/build_matsim_run_inputs.py:274A transit vehicle type outside the four-entry FLEET_CAPACITY map keeps pt2matsim's generic default capacity; it is collected into unpatched_types and printed, never refused.A future feed carries a `Metro` or `CableCar` route type. Its vehicle type is not in FLEET_CAPACITY, so it runs at pt2matsim's default seats and standing room. Crowding is inert for that mode for the whole arm, its boardings are unconstrained, and the only trace is one line of build stdout nobody re-reads.open
risksrc/build/build_activity_chains.py:759If params/C2_network_factors.json is absent, the day-type shape falls back to a typed {WEEKDAY: 1.0, SAT: 0.95, SUN: 0.80} that is in no registry field, and the source string is set to 'assumed - C2 factors file not found'.C2 is not rebuilt after a counts re-download (it is a derived file and gitignored). The chain build succeeds, Saturday demand is generated at an assumed 0.95 of weekday instead of the measured ratio, and the only evidence is a source string inside the build report - not a refusal, not a check. Every SAT and SUN arm built from it is scored against the same targets as a measured one.open
risksrc/build/build_matsim_network.py:385The emitted mapper config annotates PublicTransitMapping.numOfThreads as 'RUN.machine.threads for this build', but the value passed is the --threads CLI argument, whose default is 2 (:542). The note in a committed config records a provenance that is not true.Someone reproducing the network build reads the config's own note, sets RUN.machine.threads and gets no change, because only --threads moves it. Worse, the note asserts registry provenance for a value the registry never supplied, which is exactly the class of claim the project's provenance rules exist to prevent.open
risksrc/build/build_matsim_network.py:419Wall-clock gtfs_seconds and mapping_seconds (:423, :434) are written into networks/matsim/_matsim_build_report.json, a file the manifest hashes.A byte-identical rebuild of the network on a faster machine produces a different _matsim_build_report.json, a different sha256, a MANIFEST.csv row that no longer matches, and check_manifest.py fails in CI on a change that moved no data. The determinism rule is defeated by a timing field nobody needs in a hashed artefact.open
risksrc/build/build_manifest.py:394os.walk's subdirectory order is left unsorted (only `names` is sorted, :395), so MANIFEST.csv row ORDER is filesystem-dependent, while :439 stamps datetime.now() into the committed MANIFEST.json.The manifest is regenerated on a machine whose filesystem enumerates directories differently. Every data byte is identical but the CSV row order changes, so the diff is 500 lines of noise and a reviewer cannot see which row actually moved. MANIFEST.json additionally changes on every run regardless.open

Also read: all 55 filenames under cities/newcastle/overlays/runs/ and the RUN.* declarations for machine.threads, machine.replanning_threads, machine.seed, storage.raw_cap_gb and monitor.pace_band_s out of cities/newcastle/registry/RUN_execution.json. UNREAD: src/run/run_failure.py (346) and src/setup/dump_matsim_params.py (218), and ~900 lines in the middle of run_matsim.py (build_config's body :265-449, find_completed :678-748, mark_dead/reconcile_stale :797-922, the post-launch wait loop :1440-1553). Of the unread, run_failure.py carries a code_metrics row (from_log, 107 lines) and dump_matsim_params.py carries an unused import (sys, :33); build_config carries the second-longest function in the file (179 lines). Those rows are reported from the metrics, not from a read, and say so.

A single-owner design that has been repaired repeatedly and carries its repairs as comments. run.py is a thin front door that makes exactly one defaulting decision and says so loudly; run_matsim.py owns run identity (a parameter set plus a controler sha256, not a name), the directory naming, the meta card and the terminal record; results_store.py is the sole composer of results/ paths; src/city.py is the sole resolver of city paths. The strongest idea in the layer is the two-file record contract - _meta.json is the live status card written at launch and updated at every transition, _run.json is the terminal record whose `completion` field (not its mere presence) is the result gate - and it is honoured by find_completed, calibrate.py:304 and build_fit_figures.py:170. Concurrency is deliberate and mostly bounded: the gate watcher, the progress digest, the live view and the raw-cache trim all run as daemon threads whose failures are swallowed so they cannot kill a healthy arm. The layer's residual weaknesses are all at boundaries: an operator stop and the harness's own close-out take different paths and only one of them produces the artefact trim keeps a directory for; the store's liveness test knows the harness pid but not the JVM pid; the toolchain root and two of the calibration subprocess paths are still resolved against the working directory; and the signals compile path has no equivalent of session_gate's arm-running refusal.

Those are reported from the metrics rows, and each says so.

Two layers with one contract between them. extract_metrics.py turns a run directory into _metrics.json - modelled quantities only, and its docstring says so - and fit.py turns _metrics.json plus the CALIBRATION half of validation_targets.csv into _fit.json, with account_for_the_rest asserting that every calibration target is either scored or explained (the reconciliation is asserted, not assumed, and the docstring records the earlier cut that scored 35 of 67 and looked complete). Around that sit readers: report_mode_ridership.py is the twelve-mode view a person and the gate watcher both use, build_status_board.py regenerates the board's blocks from it, build_run_index.py catalogues every run with its completion and cause, arm_cost.py prices the next arm from the last one. The discipline about what counts as a result is genuinely present and unevenly applied: calibrate.py:304-309 and build_fit_figures.py:170-178 both REFUSE a run whose completion is not ran_to_last_iteration, build_run_index.py:116-126 carries the field through to the index, and arm_cost.py:86-114 prices on reached_iteration - but report_mode_ridership.py and build_status_board.py, the two things that produce the numbers a reader actually sees, carry no such guard. The layer's other weakness is that it re-reads: output_trips is streamed four times and output_legs twice to build one _metrics.json, and report() rebuilds its targets on every call.

Those rows are reported from the metrics, and say so. tests/check_package.py being unread is this area's largest blind spot: it is the only check that sees the full package and it is 21% of the area's lines.

A layered contract with a genuine separation between the portable half (config/schema/: what shape a field, a city descriptor, an overlay and each emitted record must be) and the city half (cities/<city>/registry/: 480 declared values, cities/<city>/tests/: the doc-shape and doc-currency claims). Around it sit checks of three kinds - resolver integrity (registry/__init__.validate plus check_registry_rules.py), declaration completeness (check_hardcoding.py, check_city.py, check_legacy_drift.py, check_matsim_defaults.py) and document truthfulness (check_doc_currency.py, check_doc_shape.py) - and three gates that run them (nine CI jobs, session_gate.py locally, and a PreToolUse hook that blocks a PR while either document gate is red). The design's strongest idea is that the checks are themselves declarative and city-owned: doc_currency.json and doc_shape.json live under cities/<city>/tests/ so the harness names no city, no document and no number; check_hardcoding's config_reach actually IMPORTS the run-input builder and emits a config to prove a field reaches MATSim. Its recurring weakness is that each check's reach is narrower than its name, and the gap is never stated in the check's own output: the city-free test looks only for place names, the city-agnosticism gate exercises only the resolver and the emitter, the legacy-drift check compares nothing, config_reach proves reach on one scenario and one day type, and the hardcoding scanner cannot see a value that is lower-case, built by a call, or a pair. The one check that DOES declare its own vacuousness - check_legacy_drift's NOTHING TO COMPARE message - is the model the others should follow, and it still exits 0 under a CI step titled as a pass.

THREE of the unread carry code_metrics rows: reader_shapes.py residence_marginals (62 lines, complexity 24, 2 nested loops), extract_hts.py (concat in a loop at :80, iterrows at :100 and :116, docstring coverage 1.00), extract_census.py (5 prints in library code, docstring coverage 0.00). reader_shapes.py going unread is the real blind spot: it is the declared reader shim every framework measurement goes through, and its failure mode (residence_marginals returning None) is cited in the Build layer findings from the CALLER's side only.

Two halves with different characters. The fetch half (fetch_abs_dem, fetch_open_data, fetch_gtfs, fetch_licences, overpass) downloads into an immutable data/raw/ tree and writes a provenance_*.json beside it recording source URL, retrieval date, sha256 and licence; the extract half (extract_zones, extract_census, extract_hts, extract_speed_zones, slice_newcastle, the two counts extractors) clips national and state datasets down to this city. Between them and the framework sits reader_shapes.py, which is the area's best idea: every framework measurement asks _city.readers() for a declared shape rather than a published column name, so measure_network_factors.py:297 can say it 'sees only the declared columns of config/schema/reader_shapes.json'. The extent problem the project's own CLAUDE.md names as its cautionary tale is genuinely fixed - overpass.py:70-99 derives the harvest bbox from the dissolved LGA boundary or from the observed corridor stop set, and refuses rather than guessing when the stop set is empty. What has not moved is everything downstream of the extent: the Opal and RMS slices are still selected by hand-typed name lists matched as substrings, the CRS is typed in three adapters while city.crs() exists, and eleven of the fourteen modules execute their whole pipeline at import with no main(), so none can be imported, tested or dry-run. The manifest is the area's contract and it is strong on hashes and licences and weak on the other four columns.

UNREAD: CitysimControler.java (646, its assemble method is 503 lines and the second-longest in the repository), GatedSubtourModeChoice.java (572, three nested 208-214-line methods), TramPriorityController.java (798), SignalsAssemblyProbe.java (613), TramPriorityProbe.java (495), the eleven ConfigGroup classes (2,657 lines between them), the eight probe/scan classes (~1,900), BikeStressScoring/BikeStressDisutility (352), ActivityLinkAssigner (195), HouseholdVehicleRoster (161), AvailabilityModesCalculator (132), RemodeRestore (128), PtSubmodeMainModeIdentifier (90), and the rest. FOUR of the unread carry code_metrics long_method rows: CitysimControler.assemble (:143, 503 lines), GatedSubtourModeChoice.getPlanAlgoInstance/PlanAlgorithm/run (:357/:359/:361, 214/211/208), SubtourChainScan.main (:66, 186), TramPriorityController.simulationInitialized (:168, 59 - under threshold). CitysimControler.assemble is the single most important unread thing in this area: it is where every extension is bound, and a binding decision there is not visible from any file I did read.

Twenty-two extension classes plus eleven config groups and a dozen probes, bound by CitysimControler.assemble under representation gates that let each mechanism be inert without being removed - the same pattern the Python side uses for A.signals.representation and A.gradient.representation. The design discipline that stands out is the RESTORE contract: an extension that mutates a selected plan during BeforeMobsim is expected to give it back at AfterMobsim, and RemodeRestore exists as a named class for exactly that, with RidePairingEngine calling restore() at four sites and reporting how many legs it restored. Thread safety is handled by declaration rather than by locks, and where it is declared it is exemplary: RunTelemetry.java:95-115 states in its own Javadoc that it has no thread safety, names the sim-step barrier as the happens-before edge, names the registry field that requires it, and points at the Python refusal that enforces the combination before the JVM starts. Determinism is taken seriously - there are no static mutable fields anywhere in the 51 files, exactly one Random and it is seeded on globalRandomSeed plus the iteration, and the one place a thread count enters the random sequence is documented in a fifteen-line comment. The area's weaknesses are three: one mutation that is not restored, one thread-count dependency that IS the random sequence, and a second class with the telemetry barrier's exact dependency that neither the registry field nor the Python refusal names.

testability
No JVM unit test exists anywhere in the repository - there is no JUnit dependency, no test source root under src/java or src/java_signals, and no Maven test phase in the run-stack build. What stands in for it is a suite of twelve standalone PROBE classes (GatedSubtourProbe, RemodeRestoreProbe, PtFareProbe, GradientTableProbe, NestedSubtourProbe, SubtourChainScan, ScatsPriorityProbe, SignalsAssemblyProbe, TramPriorityProbe and three more), each with a main() that builds a toy scenario, runs it and prints one JSON line, driven by src/run/run_signal_probes.py for the signals half. That is a real and unusually disciplined answer to a hard problem - the probes are the reason several of these mech

risksrc/java/citysim/RidePairingEngine.java:1103routeDetour writes the detour permanently into the DRIVER's selected plan at BeforeMobsim - route.setLinkIds(:1103), route.setDistance(:1104), route.setTravelTime(:1105) and leg.setTravelTime(:1106) - and nothing restores it. restore() is called at :605, :806 and :945 for RIDE legs only, and notifyAfterMobsim (:1176-1225) restores only the forced-walk remodes through RemodeRestore.A driver detours to pick up a passenger in iteration N. The detour is now the driver's plan. In iteration N+1 the pairing is not made (the passenger replanned to PT, or the endpoint rule rejects it), but the driver's route still carries the detour links and the inflated travel time, so the driver drives a trip nobody asked for and is scored for it. Over iterations the driver's plan accumulates detours the co-evolutionary loop never chose, and because the plan is the selected plan the score feedsopen

Where an iteration goes

mobsimprepareForMobsimreplanningbeforeMobsimListenersiterationEndsListeners
Phase shares of a median iteration, by sample fraction and stack. The story of the last week is the shift from a listener-dominated iteration (F23: beforeMobsimListeners 0.562) to a mobsim-dominated one (HEAD: mobsim 0.696, prepareForMobsim 0.156, replanning 0.127, our own listeners 0.005). That is the healthy shape: what is left is MATSim's own work.
Median seconds per iteration at the 25% sample, newest family last. Arms in blue, probes in amber — probe iterations run 20–30% below an arm's own (F27's probes 264–272 s against its arm's 322–349 s), which is why the honest forward band is wider than the newest probe alone.
Departures simulated per second of wall clock. The per-link tables of §9.154 move the same overlay from 1,646 to 2,378 departures a second.
Mobsim seconds against thread count on a 24-core host. 2.4× the threads buys 5.6% — the mobsim is saturated, and raising the thread count is not a lever.
The largest run directories. Two log-storm arms — F23 and F22 — hold 336.4 GiB of a 452 GiB store between them and carry no finding that results/processed does not already keep.
The finding that costs money today

At this commit, python src/analyse/arm_cost.py --iterations 250 --fraction 0.25 quotes 26.3 hours, and the launcher prints that line before every arm. It is priced on aborted_20260907T150816_300it_25pct at 376.4 s an iteration — a 23-iteration arm that predates the §9.154 repair and ran beside a stray one-core Python process. The two runs that do carry the repair are excluded by arm_cost.py:131 because they hold a profile.jfr. So the instrument built to stop the project quoting stale costs is itself quoting a stale cost, and the operator's next stated-cost approval would be asked for 8–12 hours that the model no longer needs. One unprofiled four-iteration probe, about 35 minutes, corrects it.

The 250-iteration verdict

Reachable inside a day at the measured pace, and the pace is the best this project has ever recorded. HEAD's plain iteration is 205.5 s with the flight recorder in its own clock (20260907T192715_4it_25pct, iterations 2 and 3, 25 %, 16 threads, 40 g) and ~190 s without it, against 310 s on the sibling probe taken fifty minutes earlier and 639 s at F23 a week ago. Straight through, 250 iterations at 190 s is 47,500 s = 13.2 h, plus ~7 min of setup and three milestone iterations at roughly 1.6x a plain one - call it 13.5 h. But probe iterations 2-3 are early iterations, and in the one family where a probe and an arm both exist the arm ran 20-30 % above its probes (f27_timing_probe 264-272 s against the F27 arm's own 322-349 s, 9.147/9.148), so the honest band for 250 iterations at HEAD is 13.5-18 h - against the 26.3 h that `python src/analyse/arm_cost.py --iterations 250 --fraction 0.25` quotes at this commit, because it can only price on aborted_20260907T150816_300it_25pct, a 23-iteration arm from before the repair that ran beside a stray one-core python. The cheapest thing in this report is therefore one unprofiled four-iteration probe, about thirty-five minutes, which would make the launcher tell the truth. What would HALVE it is still not on the table: at HEAD the plain iteration is 70 % mobsim, 16 % MATSim's own PersonPrepareForSim over all 154,347 persons and 13 % replanning; our own listeners are 1.0 s of it; the mobsim is measured saturated (2.4x the threads bought 5.6 %); GC is 0.78-1.02 % of wall on the first GC logs ever taken, so the heap is not a lever; the fraction is fixed by the 1 September directive and 1 % is ruled unusable. The two named remaining levers - NetworkDirectWalkPtRouter.calcRoute at 8.2 % and the ~10 % that TravelTimeCalculator still pays for representing two level crossings as a time-variant network across 143,891 links - are ~18 % together, not 50 %. Halving 190 s would need ~95 s that no measured lever offers; the only candidate large enough is a contracted routing graph for the A* that both the router and PersonPrepareForSim pay, which nobody has costed and which opens a family. And the real risk to GOAL.md requirement 8 is unchanged for a seventh consecutive family: no arm has been allowed past iteration 100 in any of the 158 runs on disk, so convergence, the innovation-off tail's pace from iteration 240 and the shape of the last 150 iterations remain unmeasured - the horizon is costed entirely from innovating iterations near the start of a run.

Phase 8 · milestones against the goal

Seven of ten hard requirements met; the two that define the twin are not

The ten hard requirements are set in cities/newcastle/docs/GOAL.md. Seven are met and dated. One is partial. The two that decide whether this is a digital twin at all — every mode inside 10% and convergence within 250 iterations — are unmet and unmeasured respectively, and they have been for the whole 28 days.

The shape of the gap

Requirement 8 is not failing — it has never been tested. Every one of the 30 comparability families since F4 stopped before it could be. Of 158 runs, five completed as arms, and the deepest reading in the project is iteration 100. The instrument that would answer it exists and has been built twice over; what has never been bought is an uninterrupted 300-iteration arm.

Phase 6 · the field, from the standing reference library

Forty-six comparable city models, and an empty top rung

The survey is not re-walked each pass. It lives in docs/reports/reference/field-survey.json, and this pass re-searched not one stored row — all 46 project rows and 12 platform rows were inside both freshness horizons (180 days for facts, 90 for liveness). The budget went where the library said it should: to its own recorded gaps. 35 of 40 calls over 5 rounds, stopped by the two-empty-rounds rule rather than by the budget.

each with its reason, so no later pass pays to rule it out again
The highest validation rung each of the 46 projects reaches. Counting cars is what the field calls validation — 24 of 46 stop at road link counts, 9 at survey shares, 7 make no validation claim at all, and 6 reach transit ridership. The rung this project is aiming at is empty, and this project is not on it either.

What the comparison says

  • The top rung is empty at 46 rows: not one surveyed project publishes a per-mode fit for every mode it simulates. This project is alone in attempting it for twelve modes - and at HEAD it reaches none of them inside 10%, reading an aborted run at iteration 20.
  • The ladder's mass sits low: 24 of 46 projects stop at road link counts, 9 at survey shares only, 6 reach transit ridership counts, and 7 make no validation claim at all. Counting cars is what the field calls validation.
  • The agencies, not the academics, set the standard this project has not yet met: MWCOG's Gen3 ActivitySim publishes acceptance criteria against 7,889 directional count links plus WMATA/MARC/VRE boardings; SEMCOG built automated calibration tooling AND a sensitivity programme; ARC calibrates on its own 2011 household survey and 2019 on-board transit survey.
  • Sample fraction is where every comparable buys its speed - 1% (Sao Paulo, the Montreal LLM study) and 10% (Nelson Mandela Bay) are ordinary. This project's 25% standing directive is at the high end of the survey, and the ~22 h, 300-iteration arm is what it costs.
  • No comparable declares its inputs the way this project does: 480 registry fields, each with units, provenance and a sweep or a held-fixed rule, checked at 0 hard-coded values. The survey's projects put their coefficients in scripts and their provenance in prose.
  • The engines are consolidating: MATSim (GNU GPL per its pom.xml, annual April release, 2026 Spring on 10 April) carries 20 of the surveyed city models, and eqasim - the only published pipeline that builds a scenario from raw open data end to end, as this project's build layer does - shipped v2.2.0 on 3 June 2026.
  • The commercial platforms lead on operation, not on fit: Aimsun Live is the only surveyed twin running live against an operating network with a published operational outcome, and PTV Visum 2026 has only just added an ABM population synthesiser. Nobody sells a per-mode calibrated multimodal twin.
  • The LLM lane still validates against traces rather than ridership: eight generative-agent projects reach no rung on this ladder, and the two that do (GTA on MiD shares plus four Berlin count stations) get there by borrowing the classical targets. The lane's stopping rule has now been met three passes running.

What each does best that we lack

projectwhat it does bestwhat we lack
MWCOG / TPB Gen3 ActivitySim (Washington DC)Publishes acceptance criteria per validation target - a stated tolerance for each of 7,889 directional count links, HPMS VMT, and WMATA/MARC/VRE boardings - inside a dated calibration and validation report.We have one blanket gate (10% per mode, 20% stop bar) and no per-target acceptance standard, and no published validation report to hold ourselves to.
SEMCOG ActivitySim (Detroit, RSG)Automated calibration tools plus a designed sensitivity programme: the model's response to demographic, land-use, infrastructure and cost changes is checked for reasonableness, not just its fit.Our calibration is hand-steered family by family, and we test sensitivity only where a registry sweep happens to be exercised - never as a programme.
eqasim (ETH IVT / IRT SystemX)A released, versioned, re-pointable pipeline - v2.2.0 on 3 June 2026 - that turns raw public data into a runnable scenario for a new city.Our build layer is city-agnostic by construction and gated as such, but it is unreleased, unversioned and has never been pointed at a second city.
POLARIS (Argonne, Chicago)Demand and supply in ONE process, so an iteration is cheap enough to reach a long horizon on a regional population, and its 2026 case study projects to 2050.Our iteration is ~205 s after this week's gradient-table work - still above the 120 s directive - and no arm since F4 has reached its declared horizon.
Aimsun Live (Aimsun)Runs live against the operating network and publishes an operational outcome (Tees Valley, 14% delay reduction) rather than a fit statistic.No live-data feedback loop at all: every target we score against is a static observation, and nothing in the model is corrected by today's network.
MATSim-NYC (NYU C2SMART)Uses INRIX speeds to calibrate unsaturated road speeds and AADT to calibrate capacities, then validates on subway ridership and traffic volumes - observation on both sides of the supply model.We have no observed speed in the calibration loop; capacities and free speeds are declared, and only ridership is scored.
ActivitySim (consortium)An estimation mode: an agency re-estimates the model components on its own household travel survey rather than borrowing coefficients (SANDAG ABM3 on the 2022 HTS).The NSW HTS is aggregate-only, so our behavioural coefficients are borrowed from literature and swept - the single largest un-derived block in the model.
Washington DC MATSim open-data study (Ruan et al., 2025)Validates the same model against TWO different worlds - pre-COVID and during-COVID ground-truth flows - so the claim is about response, not only level.We score one base day against one set of targets; nothing in the twin has been asked to reproduce a change we already observed.

Couplings published to MAT

Where our row sits

Our row, filled from the artefacts only

Engine MATSim end to end, with two of our own contribs (ride pairing, SCATS signals). City Newcastle NSW, five LGAs, 1,500 core SA1s, 622,036 synthetic persons. Sample 25% by standing directive — the high end of a field where 1% and 10% are ordinary. Modes twelve, all physically simulated or explicitly priced. Signals SCATS implemented as its published algorithm at 14 corridor intersections. Validation rung attempted per-mode ridership, every mode — the empty rung. Validation rung reached none: in calibration, no mode inside 10%. What we do that nobody in the survey does declare every controllable value — 480 registry fields with units, provenance and a sweep or a held-fixed rule, with hard-coding gated at 0 in CI.

Phase 7 · what a decision simulator must contain

Seventy-two factors, thirty-seven of them fully in the model

The literature half of every row is reused from docs/reports/reference/factors.json under a 365-day horizon — a meta-analysis says the same thing this week as last. The status half is never reused. All 72 statuses were re-read at f40d332 this pass by grep of the registry and the Java, because the model moves weekly and a status carried forward is a status that is wrong. 21 of 40 calls over 6 rounds went to the five rows whose literature half was still empty; three closed.

IN — present and reaching the run PARTIAL — present, incomplete INERT — declared in the registry, read by nothing ASC — folded into a mode constant OUT — absent
Coverage at HEAD: IN 37 · PARTIAL 27 · INERT 2 · ASC 1 · OUT 5. Against af7d718 six hours earlier (IN 35 · PARTIAL 28 · INERT 1 · ASC 2 · OUT 6), route choice moved PARTIAL→IN on RUN.travel_time.filter_modes, and two factors were newly proven INERT.

What would move the scoreboard

Ranked by strength of evidence × relevance to a deviation the board carries today × how much of the data is already in the package.

#factormodedeviation nowwhy it would movedata already held
1Crowding (seated / standing)heavy_rail+417.1%The largest deviation on the board has no brake. Capacity binds physically - all four fleet types were patched from published seated/standing figures - but C.crowding.seated_multiplier and standing_multiplier carry no matsim_param and no consumer, and build_matsim_run_inputs.py:1212 lists them as not representable. The literature is unambiguous and quantified (a standing multiplier around 1.4-1.5 on in-vehicle time), the coefficients are already declared with sweeps, and nothing about the demand or the network changes.Everything: published seated/standing capacities for tram, bus, ferry and rail are in the registry and patched into the run vehicles; the two multipliers are declared (1.0 / 1.45). Only a capacity-dependent scoring extension in src/java/citysim is missing.
2Reliability and headwaybus+106.9%Bus is at more than double its target while light_rail is 30% under - a service-quality inversion. The model charges a half-hourly bus minute exactly what it charges a frequent tram minute, because C.time_weights.beta_headway and beta_reliability are written to params/C1_parameters.json (src/build/build_params.py:99-100) and read by nothing in the run. This is a proven INERT pair, not a suspicion.Both coefficients are declared with values and sweeps; headways are already derivable per route from the mapped GTFS (src/analyse/measure_corridor_composition.py:191 computes headway_stats today).
3Replication across seeds / run-to-run noiselight_rail-30.0%Every deviation on the board is quoted without an error bar, and a MATSim run here is not bit-reproducible (DECISIONS 3.5). E.replication.n_replications = 30 is declared and the phys1000_arm_b_25pct overlay's own record says no seed-variance measurement exists yet. Until it does, a -30.0% light_rail reading and a -13.0% car reading cannot be distinguished from noise, and every other recommendation in this ledger is ranked on numbers with unknown precision.The mechanism exists - RUN.machine.seed moves both the household draw and MATSim's global seed. It costs run time, not data: two arms at the same identity.
4Person attributes: age and sexbike+198.4%The literature magnitude lands exactly on the two worst active-mode deviations: women are about half as likely to cycle as men and about 23% more likely to walk (Goel et al. 2022, 19 cities / 13 countries). This model applies ONE cycling propensity to both sexes - the sex attribute is on every synthetic person but reaches nothing in behaviour, appearing only in src/analyse/measure_demographic_modes.py. Halving one sex's cycling propensity is the mechanism a +198.4% overshoot is shaped like.The sex attribute is already written for every agent and B.population.bike_available_rate = 0.493 is already a swept field; the change is a per-attribute availability or scoring term, with no acquisition.
5In-vehicle time and value of time by purposebus+106.9%Six purpose-specific values of time are declared (HW 18.6, HE 9.3, WB 55.4 AUD/h among them) and the assembler collapses them to one trip-weighted average, saying so in the run report at build_matsim_run_inputs.py:1209-1211. One traveller type who is uniformly time-rich is the simplest explanation for bus and heavy_rail overshooting together while car undershoots.All six values, their sources and their sweeps are in cities/newcastle/registry/C_behaviour.json; MATSim subpopulation scoring is already used for income, so the mechanism is in place.
6Light rail: tram priority, dwelllight_rail-30.0%The only PT mode running BELOW target, and the mechanism that would raise it is written, registered and switched off: src/java_signals/citysim/TramPriorityController.java is bound at CitysimSignalsControler.java:101-102 while A.lightrail.tsp_enabled = False. A.signals.tsp.mode = green_extension and priority_group = tram are already declared. This is the shortest distance in the whole ledger between coded capability and board movement.Entirely: the controller, the signals stack (.tools/classes-signals is built), and all seven A.signals.tsp.* fields. It is a boolean and a family boundary.
7Workplace locationwalk+64.7%Commute distance is what separates a car trip from a walk trip, and this model draws destinations from a solved gravity decay with no journey-to-work flow check at all. Walk +64.7%, bike +198.4% and bus +106.9% are all consistent with work being placed too close to home; car -13.0% is the mirror. STATUS.md already names "inter-LGA commute flows" as an open assessment finding, and the field validates this with an LGA-to-LGA flow table as standard practice.The census journey-to-work flow table is already used - B.external.interaction_rate was DERIVED from the 2011 flow (DECISIONS 9.140) - and cities/newcastle/build/map_sa1_to_lga.py already carries the SA1->LGA join. The check is a script over an existing artefa
8Choice-set generation and mode availabilitybike+198.4%RUN.mode_choice.modes contains six of the twelve modes - car, ride, pt, bike, walk, taxi - so 100% of the choosable mass is fought over by six alternatives while motorbike, truck and freight are carved deterministically. Four of the six overshoot (walk, taxi, bike, bus) and two undershoot (car, ride): the residual has literally nowhere else to go. This is the structural reason the ASCs will have to absorb specification error.AvailabilityModesCalculator and GatedSubtourModeChoice already gate per person and per subtour, and B.motorbike.trip_share is measured from census G62; making motorbike choosable is a Java and registry change, not an acquisition. It opens a family.
9Intra-zonal tripswalk+64.7%The registry itself records the model generating 4.45% of legs under 1 km against the HTS table's 18.8% (issue #30). A model short of sub-kilometre trips must satisfy the observed active share on LONGER legs - which is exactly what a +64.7% walk share and a +198.4% bike share look like on a linked-trip basis.HTS Sydney 2012/13 Table 4.4.7 is already the basis of B.activity.short_trip_band_share, and the mixture weight is already solved against it; the gap is in what the solve achieves, and it is measurable from the run's own trips table.
10Taxi / rideshare: wait, fleet, refusal, surgetaxi+105.6%Taxi is at more than double its target with a finite fleet that already refuses (TaxiFleetEngine.java:62 walks a refused request). So the missing suppressant is price, not supply: there is no surge (grep returns nothing) and, with the income exponent at 1.0 and no per-purpose VOT, a metered fare feels the same to everyone. C.taxi.asc and C.taxi.wait_min are both declared and swept.The metered fares (flagfall and per-km for both taxi and rideshare) and the fleet parameters are all declared; a surge multiplier would be a new field with a stated sweep, since no Newcastle surge series is published.
The two-line summary of the factor ledger

The largest deviation on the board — heavy rail at +417.1% — has no brake at all: capacity binds physically because every fleet type was patched from published seated and standing figures, but the crowding disutility does not exist, and build_matsim_run_inputs.py:1212 lists it as not-representable. The mode running furthest below target, light rail at −30.0%, has its mechanism written, registered and switched off: TramPriorityController.java is bound and A.lightrail.tsp_enabled is False. That is the shortest distance in this ledger between code that already exists and a number on the board.

The ledger, by decision horizon

A. Long-term choices — 7 factors

factorwhat the research saysmagnitudehow the leading simulators do itstatus hereproof at HEADwhat it would move
Residential location (fixed from census)Residential self-selection is a measured but minority share of the built-environment effect: disentangling it by housing type in one study put self-selection at 15.2%, 30.7%, 18.5% and 5.9% of the total impact on vehicle kilometres travelled for the four housing types examined, and the effect is modest for the elderly and large for younger adults. The built-environment side remains the Ewing-Cervero meta-analysis, with every 5D elasticity inelastic. A residence fixed from the census therefore carries most of the buliterature: self-selection 6-31% of the total built-environment effect on VKT, varying by housing type; the remainder is the location itselfUrbanSim-class land-use models re-choose residence; ActivitySim, CT-RAMP, MATSim and eqasim all take residence from the synthetic population and never re-choose it during a run.INsrc/build/build_population.py:244 places every synthetic person in an SA1 against D1_zone_attractions_SA1.csv; cities/newcastle/build/map_sa1_to_lga.py carries the SA1->LNothing directly - homes are fixed from the census and are not a free parameter. It bounds every other layer: the SA1 placement decides the distance distribution that walk (+64.7%) and bike (+198.4%) are drawn on.
Workplace locationWorkplace location is a calibrated long-term choice in every activity-based practice: ActivitySim samples commute distances from regional distributions and selects zones to match them under land-use compatibility, then validates residence-to-work flows against the census commuting-flow table and the mandatory trip-length frequency distribution; where attractions are more reliable than the impedance the practice is doubly constrained (shadow-priced) so that both worker totals and job totals are held. The output checunknown as a coefficient: the practice benchmark is an origin-destination flow table (census journey-to-work) and a trip-length distribution, not a central tendencyActivitySim and CT-RAMP run a shadow-priced work location choice validated against census commuting flows; MATSim scenarios assign workplaces in the demand builder and hold them fixed.PARTIALDestinations are drawn from a solved gravity decay over D1 attractions (src/build/build_activity_chains.py:410, :253) and the external tier from B.external.commute_share_Commute distance is what separates a car trip from a walk trip. Car sits at -13.0% while walk is +64.7% and bike +198.4%: if work is being placed too close to home, short active trips are being manufactured out of commutes that should be car or bus (+106.9%).
Vehicle ownership per householdHousehold car ownership is one of the strongest single predictors of mode: an increase in car ownership raises the probability of commuting by car and depresses active and transit modes, with a reported elasticity of -2.643 for the substitution of active modes. Income, household size, distance to centre, accessibility to shops/services/employment and intersection density are the dominant explanatory variables.literature: elasticity of active-mode use with respect to car ownership approximately -2.6; income and household size the leading sociodemographic driversActivitySim/CT-RAMP run an explicit auto-ownership choice model calibrated to observed auto sufficiency; MATSim scenarios usually take vehicles from the synthetic population and enforce availability through chain-based mode constraints rather than re-choosing INB.population.vehicle_roster -> src/java/citysim/HouseholdVehicleRoster.java, bound at src/java/citysim/CitysimControler.java:471-472Ride is -45.2%: the roster decides which household member can hold the car and therefore who must be a passenger. Raising or lowering ownership moves the driver/passenger split directly.
Vehicle type (EV, e-bike)The e-bike evidence is now meta-analysed: across experimental studies, access to an e-bike adds about 5 km of daily travel and raises e-bike mode share by about 26 percentage points, while car use falls by about 2.4 km a day (a 10% drop in car mode share); single controlled trials report car share falling 21%, and older meta-studies put e-bike-for-car substitution at 43% of trips and 63% of mileage. The effect is context-dependent: where cycling is already high the e-bike substitutes conventional cycling; where it literature: +5 km/day travelled and +26 pp e-bike share with e-bike access; car -2.4 km/day (~-10% car share); substitution 43% of car trips in earlier synthesesMATSim's bicycle contrib carries an e-bike as a vehicle type with its own speed and gradient response; no production city model draws an e-bike or EV ownership decision - both enter as a share of the fleet.OUTNo registry field and no code: grep -rE "electric|ev_share|e_bike|ebike|pedelec" over src, cities/newcastle/build and the registry returns only a sweep_basis string aboutAn e-bike raises the tolerable cycling distance and gradient. Bike is +198.4% - too MANY bike trips - so adding e-bikes would push the same direction and is not the repair; it matters for a later scenario, not for closing the present deviation.
Licence holdingLicence holding among people under 35 has fallen across Australia, the UK, the US, Canada and much of Europe: TfNSW reports 65.4% of 16-20 year olds licensed in 2017, 8.3 points below 2001 and 8.1 below 2009, with the proportion licensed at age 30 also declining cohort on cohort. The travel-behaviour consequence named is a greater reliance on getting a lift, especially in wealthy suburbs and high-car-ownership families, and more public transport, walking and cycling in less wealthy areas.literature: 16-20 licence rate 65.4% (2017 NSW), down ~8 points on 2001; effect is a shift toward being a car passenger and toward PT/active modesActivitySim/CT-RAMP treat licence holding inside the auto-ownership and person-type models; MATSim scenarios encode it as a person attribute gating car as a chain-based mode.INB.population.licence_rate_by_age_band, built by cities/newcastle/build/build_licence_rates.py from the published count (DECISIONS 9.131); read by src/build/build_matsim_pA non-licence-holder cannot drive, so the licence rate sets the ceiling on car (-13.0%) and the floor on ride (-45.2%) and bus (+106.9%). It is measured, so it is a constraint rather than a lever.
Public-transport passes / concessionsA smartcard natural experiment on Dutch fares separates pass holders from single-ticket users: passengers on a monthly or annual subscription have the highest travel frequency per origin-destination pair per week - almost twice that of single-ticket users - and the estimated fare elasticities split cleanly between the frequent-user products (pay-as-you-go, student and subscription) and the occasional ones (end-of-month and single tickets). A pass converts the fare from a per-trip price to a zero marginal cost, and literature: subscription holders travel about 2x as often per OD pair as single-ticket users; fare elasticity differs by product classActivitySim/CT-RAMP carry a per-person fare class or pass flag into the cost term; MATSim fare handlers (as here) price per trip and per day-cap, so a pass has to be expressed as a zero marginal fare for the holder.PARTIALAge concessions ARE priced - A.fare.child_min_age / child_max_age / senior_min_age and the daily caps reach citysim.PtFareChargeHandler through src/build/build_matsim_runBus is +106.9% and heavy_rail +417.1%. A period pass makes the marginal journey free and would push both further up, so the missing mechanism is not the cause of the overshoot; it is a fidelity gap that will matter once the levels are near.
Bicycle ownershipOwnership is high and use is low, and the two are only weakly coupled: the National Cycling Participation Survey (2011-2019) finds more than half of Australian households own at least one bicycle while cycling is 1.4% of daily travel; Melbourne apartment households own 0.86 bicycles on average, off-street bicycle parking more than doubles the odds a household owns one, and the correlation between household bicycles and regional cycling use is 0.238. Ownership is male, younger, more educated and higher-income; rentiliterature: >50% of households own a bicycle against 1.4% cycling mode share (NCPS); 0.86 bikes per apartment household; ownership-use correlation 0.24ActivitySim implementations gate bike by a household bicycle flag where the survey carries it; MATSim scenarios (as here) draw an availability rate per person and let mode choice decide use; no production model estimates an ownership choice.INB.population.bike_available_rate = 0.493 read at src/build/build_matsim_plans.py:62 and documented as the availability gate in src/java/citysim/AvailabilityModesCalculatoBike is the worst deviation on a share basis at +198.4%. The ownership rate is the single cheapest lever: it is a declared field with a sweep, changing it needs no new data, and it multiplies the population that can choose bike at all.

B. Daily activity pattern — 6 factors

factorwhat the research saysmagnitudehow the leading simulators do itstatus hereproof at HEADwhat it would move
Activity generation and schedulingDaily travel budgets are strikingly stable: the Sydney Household Travel Survey reports an average 81 minutes travelling per person per day and 24-30 km per person per day across regions, with average travel time steady over the reporting series while mode composition moved (weekday train trips +3.1%, bus +2.4%, walk-only +2.7%, vehicle driver -0.8%, passenger -0.2%).literature: ~81 min/person/day travelling, 24-30 km/person/day (NSW HTS); the time budget is stable while mode composition movesActivitySim/CT-RAMP generate a full daily activity pattern per person from estimated models; MATSim takes chains as an input and mutates only times and modes during the run.INB.activity.hts_rate_per_person_day (src/build/build_activity_chains.py:2780), act_duration_min (:294), p_intermediate_stop (:164), day_purpose_mix (:147)The trip rate and purpose mix set the denominator every mode share is read against, so an error here moves all twelve at once. Car -13.0% and walk +64.7% are shares of exactly this total.
Joint household decisionsJoint and partially joint travel is a material share of household tours: partially joint tours - where one or more passengers is dropped off or picked up mid-tour - make up close to 14% of all tour types in metropolitan areas, and households with more than one student at the same school very commonly serve them on one car tour.literature: partially joint tours ~14% of all tour typesCT-RAMP models joint tours explicitly (participation, party composition, destination); ActivitySim carries the same joint-tour chain; MATSim has no native joint-tour construct and scenarios add it as a contrib or in the demand builder.INB.activity.joint_tour_passenger_ratio (src/build/build_activity_chains.py:217) and B.ride.joint_coherence_rate; citysim.JointRideEngine bound at src/java/citysim/CitysimCRide is -45.2%. Joint tours are where a passenger trip comes from, and the engine that physically carries them is the mechanism the F30 family was opened to test.
Escort of childrenEscorting is modelled in practice as a nested choice: school tours split into outbound and inbound half-tours, each with pure escort / ridesharing / no escort and up to three household chauffeurs. Significant determinants are the chauffeur's employment status, age and flexibility at work, the child's age, household characteristics and the relative distances between home, school and workplace; mothers working longer hours and further from home are less likely to chauffeur.literature: three escort alternatives per half-tour, up to three candidate chauffeurs; chauffeur work hours and job distance are the leading determinantsCT-RAMP and ActivitySim implement a dedicated school-escort model with chauffeur assignment; MATSim carries no escort construct natively.INB.activity.escort_binding_enabled = true (src/build/build_activity_chains.py:177), scope any_member_trip; citysim.EscortCoherenceListener bound at src/java/citysim/CitysiRide -45.2% again: the open family F30 is literally "an escort is priced as an escort" and its one boundary line is this listener's draw order.
Telework / work-from-homeTelework reduces commuting and business trips, most clearly for full-time teleworkers, but the effect on TOTAL distance is mixed and design-dependent: rebound effects (extra non-work trips) and residential relocation to longer commutes offset part of the saving, and one-worker households increase total travel - particularly by car - while two-worker households show no significant increase.literature: commute trips reduced; total distance effect ambiguous with documented rebound and relocation offsetsActivitySim implementations added post-pandemic work-from-home models as a person-level choice feeding the daily activity pattern; MATSim scenarios usually encode it by removing work activities from a share of plans.OUTgrep -rE "telework|work_from_home|wfh" over src, cities/newcastle/build, the registry and the overlays returns nothing at HEADA 2026 base year with no telework overstates commuting, which inflates car and PT trip counts. Car is -13.0% (too few), so telework is not the cause of the present car gap - but it is a named requirement of a 2026 base and its absence is undocumented in the re
Day-type differences (weekday, Saturday, Sunday)Weekend travel has a different shape, not just a different volume: the sharp early-morning and mid-afternoon weekday peaks are absent on the weekend day because so few trips are to and from work, and social-recreational and personal-business travel spread more evenly across the day become the dominant influence; weekend travel raises car-pooling for both youth and adults but has no measured effect on transit use, and destination land use shifts toward residential.literature: weekend day loses both commute peaks; purpose mix shifts to social/recreational; carpooling up, transit unchanged (NHTS 2009)CT-RAMP and ActivitySim are weekday models by default with separate weekend estimation where funded; MATSim scenarios build a weekend day from a separate plans file and timetable, as this model does for SAT and SUN.PARTIALE.matrix.day_types drives 30 scenario x day-type run-input sets and the per-day-type schedules; but B.activity.weekend_to_weekday = 0.7521 is on check_hardcoding.py's DECNothing on the current board - every gate arm is S2 x WEEKDAY. It becomes a defect the moment a Saturday arm is read, because the declared field would not be the one in force.
Mobility impairmentPeople with a travel-limiting disability are 8-10% of the population and make fewer trips - about 18.6% fewer overall in the Utah household survey, with the disparity largest on transit (4.21 against 5.71 trips a day) and smallest for driving alone - and they choose differently: a measured shift toward car-pooling, a lower value of travel time, and a transit share that stays low despite a 50% fare concession because access, not price, is the barrier.literature: ~8-10% of the population; ~19% fewer trips; transit trips 4.21 vs 5.71 per day; shift to car passengerActivitySim implementations carry a disability flag into person type where the survey supports it; MATSim scenarios seldom represent it, and this model synthesises the flag without a consumer.INERTsrc/build/build_matsim_plans.py:1087 writes a "mobilityImpaired" person attribute into every plans file; grep -rE "mobilityImpaired|mobility_impaired" over src/java, src/Walk is +64.7%. An impaired share that cannot walk far is one of the few mechanisms that removes walk trips without touching any other mode's utility. The attribute is already on every agent, so wiring it is a scoring or availability change, not a data acquisi

C. Destination choice — 4 factors

factorwhat the research saysmagnitudehow the leading simulators do itstatus hereproof at HEADwhat it would move
Attraction by purpose (jobs, floorspace, enrolments)The practice is settled on size terms: each destination alternative's utility is a set of impedance terms plus one size function, where the size term is total or industry-specific employment for work, school enrolment for education, and for non-work purposes only the relevant categories - retail employment for shopping, restaurant employment for meals - with households or population for social purposes. Estimation results then show purpose-specific impedance coefficients (e.g. -0.01 business to -0.11 daily shoppingliterature: size term = log of a weighted sum of purpose-relevant employment/enrolment/households; impedance coefficients purpose-specific, roughly -0.01 to -0.11 per minute in a reported estimationActivitySim/CT-RAMP estimate the size-term weights per purpose from the survey; MATSim demand builders (as here) declare them and validate against a job distribution.IND.attraction.job_weight_by_category and D.attraction.purpose_weight read at src/build/build_zone_attractions.py:43,45; place-of-work totals disaggregated to SA1 by a workAttractions decide where trips go and therefore how long they are. Bus +106.9% and heavy_rail +417.1% are both concentrated-destination modes: too much attraction at the interchange manufactures rail boardings.
Distance decayThe gravity/spatial-interaction relationship declines with distance, time and cost; the two competing deterrence forms are the power law and the negative exponential, with the negative exponential generally the preferred form in transport application, and the estimated deterrence parameter is sensitive to the spatial arrangement of the study area.literature: negative-exponential deterrence generally preferred over power law; parameter is context- and geometry-sensitive rather than transferableFour-step and gravity models fit a per-purpose deterrence function; ActivitySim replaces it with a logsum-based destination utility; MATSim inherits whatever the demand builder produced.INThe destination-draw decay is SOLVED per purpose against observed means (src/build/build_activity_chains.py:81-93, :253); B.freight.gravity_beta_per_km for freight (:1992Walk +64.7% and bike +198.4% are the short-distance modes; car -13.0% is the long one. The decay is the parameter that decides how much of the trip mass sits under 2 km, and it is already solved against HTS means, so a distance-band comparison is available wit
Constraints at both ends (capacity)A doubly constrained model preserves both the origin and destination totals from trip generation while a singly constrained one preserves origins only; doubly constrained is the appropriate form where the attraction totals are more reliable than the friction factors, and the standard case for work location, where predicted flows should equal both worker totals and job totals - in activity-based practice this is implemented as shadow pricing on the work and school location choices.literature: no coefficient - a structural choice; doubly constrained (shadow-priced) is standard for work and school, singly constrained for discretionary purposesActivitySim/CT-RAMP shadow-price work and school location to hit zone job and enrolment totals; MATSim demand builders (as here) balance arrivals iteratively.INB.activity.destination_balancing = "doubly_constrained" (src/build/build_activity_chains.py:266, :505) with B.activity.balancing_passes and balancing_toleranceDoubly constraining holds job totals as well as worker totals, which keeps the CBD from absorbing every commute. It bears on the heavy_rail +417.1% overshoot through interchange-bound trips.
Intra-zonal tripsShort trips are systematically undercounted in travel surveys - the undercount concentrates on short walking, cycling and car trips for shopping and leisure, and every national survey from 1977 to 2022 has undercounted total walk trips by omitting short walks to stops and car parks. More than 80% of walk trips are under 2 km, and walking and cycling behave as substitutes below 2 km.literature: >80% of walk trips are under 2 km; walk trips systematically undercounted in survey targets; walk and bike substitute below 2 kmActivitySim/CT-RAMP handle intrazonal trips with an intrazonal impedance term and micro-zone allocation; MATSim simulates them physically on the real network if the network resolution allows it.INB.activity.short_trip_band_share / short_trip_band_km / short_trip_mean_km (src/build/build_activity_chains.py:256-258) with the mixture weight solved against HTS Sydney Directly on walk (+64.7%) and bike (+198.4%): a model that is short of sub-kilometre trips has to satisfy the observed active share on LONGER legs, which is exactly the shape a +64.7% walk overshoot takes. The observed distribution is already in the package.

D. Departure time — 2 factors

factorwhat the research saysmagnitudehow the leading simulators do itstatus hereproof at HEADwhat it would move
Departure-time profile by purposeDeparture time is a genuine choice, not a fixed profile: Small (1982) tied departure-time choice to a workplace constraint in the utility function, and travellers were willing to shift one to two minutes toward the early side, or one-third to one minute toward the late side, to save one minute of travel time.literature: willingness to shift 1-2 min early, or 1/3-1 min late, per minute of travel time saved (Small 1982)ActivitySim/CT-RAMP model tour departure-time choice by purpose; MATSim mutates departure times each iteration under TimeAllocationMutator and prices the result through the scoring function.INB.activity.departure_profile read at src/build/build_activity_chains.py:319; RUN.replanning.weights gives TimeAllocationMutator 0.05 with RUN.replanning.time_mutation_ranSTATUS.md names "evening departures" as an open assessment finding. A mis-timed evening peak puts trips outside the PT timetable, which is one way bus lands at +106.9% while light_rail lands at -30.0%.
Schedule delay / activity duration preferencesThe schedule-delay cost function is asymmetric: the unit cost of arriving late exceeds the unit cost of arriving early, the disutility falls linearly to zero as arrival approaches the desired time, and Small hypothesises a FIXED penalty component on the late side - arriving late is always bad, however slightly.literature: late-arrival unit cost strictly greater than early; a fixed late penalty on top of the linear termMATSim prices exactly this pair as scoring.lateArrival and scoring.earlyDeparture against an activity's typical and opening/closing times; ActivitySim carries it inside time-of-day choice utilities.PARTIALC.scoring.activity_typical_duration_s and activity_minimal_duration_s reach scoring (src/build/build_matsim_run_inputs.py:1263-1264) and RUN.scoring.late_arrival_utils_peA late-arrival penalty that cannot fire removes the whole reason to leave early, which flattens the peak and makes the slow modes look cheap. Bus +106.9% and heavy_rail +417.1% both benefit from a world with no schedule pressure.

Parking cost and search timeUnderpriced parking generates cruising, and cruising is a large share of central-area traffic: studies between 1927 and 2001 found 3.5-14 minutes to find a curb space and 8-74% of traffic cruising, with more recent work above 70%, and search time reaching up to 40% of total travel time. Bike: stress (traffic), gradient, e-bikeCyclists trade distance for stress at large, well-measured rates: on average cyclists travel 67% longer to include a cycle path facility, weekend cyclists up to 40% longer, and cyclists accept a 25-38% detour to avoid segments with high near-crash rates. Level of Traffic Stress integrates infrastructure type, road hierarchy, traffic volume and speed limit into one indicator, alongside BCI, BSL and HCM6. H. Behavioural machinery — 5 factors

factorwhat the research saysmagnitudehow the leading simulators do itstatus hereproof at HEADwhat it would move
Utility form (Charypar-Nagel scoring)MATSim's scoring is the Charypar-Nagel form: plan utility is the sum of activity utilities plus travel disutilities, with activity utility beta_dur * t_typ * ln(t_dur / t_0) - marginal utility of duration against a typical duration and a minimal duration below which utility is negative - and leg score built from a mode constant, a marginal disutility of travel duration, and a marginal disutility of distance. Under iteration the population's average plan score stabilises at a point where individuals cannot unilateraliterature: activity utility is logarithmic in duration against a typical duration; leg score is linear in time and distance plus a mode constantMATSim and its derivatives (eqasim, BEAM) score Charypar-Nagel; ActivitySim/CT-RAMP use nested-logit utilities instead, which is a different object - a nest coefficient has no MATSim equivalent.INC.scoring.performing_utils_per_h, marginal_utility_of_traveling, monetary_distance_rate and marginal_utility_of_money assembled at src/build/build_matsim_run_inputs.py:10The utility form is the frame every deviation is expressed in. It is correctly and completely wired; the gaps in this ledger are missing TERMS (crowding, headway, per-purpose VOT), not a missing form.
Heterogeneity / value-of-time segmentsHeterogeneity in the value of time is real and income-driven, with an income elasticity of VTTS of about 0.67-0.80 - below the unity convention. Choice-set generation and mode availabilityThe choice set in an agent-based model is generated, not enumerated: MATSim's SubtourModeChoice changes the mode of all legs of one randomly chosen subtour to a randomly chosen alternative, and offers a mode only where the choice would not require a resource to appear out of thin air - chain-based modes assume one resource per mode, initially at home. Learning, replanning, plan memory, innovation switch-offThe distinction that governs convergence: while innovation is switched on - new routes, new times - the result is NOT truly stationary; if innovation is switched off the process is stationary but limited to the plans each agent holds at that moment. The board says "Not a result" for exactly this reason, and the whole ledger is read against a pre-relaxation snapshot.
LLM-driven agentsThe 2025 evidence is that LLM agents can reproduce realistic travel behaviour and system-level dynamics in morning-commute settings and can serve as the agent model inside a multi-agent simulation such as MATSim; alignment techniques - few-shot learning and travel-behaviour persona loading - materially improve mode-choice accuracy and can surpass traditional discrete choice models where domain knowledge is supplied. LLM agents partially replicate human route-switching behaviour against laboratory data.
