The manual also warns that counts themselves vary by 10% or more from daily and seasonal variation, and recommends at least one midweek 24-hour count every two years.literature: +/-9% regional transit boardings, +/-20% transit screenlines, 5%/10% screenline/cutline volume targets; count data itself carries >=10% variabilityEvery MPO model in the US validates against this manual; MATSim scenarios in the literature typically report link-count fits and rarely per-mode ridership for every mode.INcities/newcastle/build/build_mode_targets.py writes data/processed/validation/mode_targets_by_mode.csv, one row per mode, read by src/analyse/report_mode_ridership.py:87;This is the instrument the whole board is read on, and it is the project's strongest position in the surveyed field: no comparable project scores every simulated mode against its own observation. It is also why the board reads "Inside 10%: none" honestly.
Holdout enforcementValidation compares the model against information other than that used to estimate it; the common practice is a random split into estimation and holdout samples at 80/20 or 75/25, with out-of-sample performance indices computed on the withheld part, and MPO guidance asks for calibration and validation at every model step. What the guidance does not describe is enforcement - no surveyed practice makes the holdout unreadable by construction.literature: 80/20 or 75/25 estimation/holdout splits; validation on data not used in estimationStandard in estimation of choice models; conventional rather than enforced in MPO validation; not a feature of MATSim or ActivitySim tooling.INsrc/calibrate/calibrate.py:4-6 is "structurally unable to read a holdout row", with a second independent audit at :237-238 (audit_no_holdout); tests/check_package.py:169-Nothing on the board today - the holdout opens once, at the end (STATUS P5). It is what will make any eventual reading credible, and it is enforced in two independent places rather than by convention.
Convergence criterionConvergence in an iterative agent model has a precise meaning and a precise trap: the process is not stationary while innovation runs, and is stationary after switch-off only within the plans agents already hold. Empirically, between-seed variation in link loads dominates the variation between the last two iterations within one seed, so a within-run stability test alone is not evidence of convergence.literature: between-seed variation of link loads exceeds last-two-iteration within-seed variationMATSim practice reads score and mode-share stability after the innovation cutoff; ActivitySim has no iterative convergence criterion of this kind.INRUN.relaxation.drift_tolerance_pp = 0.5 and RUN.relaxation.settle_margin_iterations read at src/analyse/summarise_run.py:75-84 and plotted by src/analyse/progress_digest.The board reads at iteration 20 of a stopped arm because no arm since family F4 has reached its gate. The criterion is wired; what is missing is a run that survives long enough to test it against the GOAL.md 250-iteration requirement.
Replication across seeds / run-to-run noiseRandom seeds move agent-based results materially: across 100 seeds of one MATSim scenario, relative errors of up to 10% occur even on links with large volumes, and the variation between seeds largely dominates the variation between the two last iterations within a seed. Aggregate travel times are robust after one iteration, but disaggregate results needed about 31 simulations on average to reach a robust mean.literature: up to 10% relative link-volume error across seeds; ~31 replications for a robust disaggregate mean; between-seed >> within-seed variationAimsun and Vissim require multiple seeded replications as standard practice; most published MATSim scenarios report a single seed, which is the field's most common methodological weakness.PARTIALE.replication.n_replications = 30 is declared and reaches cities/newcastle/build/build_scenario_configs.py:40,172; RUN.machine.seed is declared "held at the master seed uEVERY deviation on the board is quoted without an error bar. A MATSim run is not bit-reproducible (DECISIONS 3.5), so a -13.0% car reading and a -30.0% light_rail reading may not be distinguishable from noise. Nothing else in this ledger can be ranked confiden
Sensitivity sweepsThe recommended method for agent-based models is variance-based global sensitivity analysis: because ABMs are non-linear, Sobol' indices decompose the output variance into first-order and total contributions of each parameter and its interactions, sampled with Sobol' sequences over the input space; one-at-a-time sweeps are the local, linear special case and miss interactions.literature: no coefficient - a method; Sobol' total-order indices over a Sobol'-sequence sample, typically hundreds to thousands of runsPublished MATSim and SUMO studies mostly do one-at-a-time sweeps of a few parameters; the ABM literature recommends Sobol' indices as routine practice.INEvery field carries a sweep, a held_fixed rule or a derived_from identity or the schema rejects it; check_hardcoding.py --strict is a CI gate reporting TOTAL 0 items at HThis is the control that makes every other row in this ledger actionable: no lever named here is a number typed into a script. It is the project's strongest process claim.
ASC calibration methodAn alternative-specific constant is the net average effect of the variables the utility omits, and calibration adjusts it iteratively - run, compare modelled to observed mode shares, move the constants, repeat until the fit is acceptable. UK TAG supplementary guidance on bespoke mode choice models is the formal statement; the risk it names is that constants absorb specification error and any new alternative has no constant to inherit.literature: no coefficient - an iterative adjustment to observed shares; the constant is the mean of the omitted variablesActivitySim/CT-RAMP calibrate ASCs to survey shares as a routine final step; MATSim scenarios adjust mode constants by hand or, as here, declare them fixed so misfit stays visible.PARTIALC.asc.car_driver (0.0, the reference), car_passenger, bus, light_rail, rail, walk, cycle map to MATSim modeParams constants at src/build/build_matsim_run_inputs.py:1088-1Ten of twelve modes are outside 10% and eight past the 20% stop bar, so the ASCs are the fastest lever on the board by construction. The risk is the same one that makes them fast: with counts out of the objective and no crowding or headway term, an ASC fit wil

J. Data — 5 factors

factorwhat the research saysmagnitudehow the leading simulators do itstatus hereproof at HEADwhat it would move
Population synthesisPopulation synthesis is the required input to any agent model because individual-level attributes for the whole population do not exist; the established techniques are iterative proportional fitting, iterative proportional updating, combinatorial optimisation, and Markov- and fitness-based synthesis. There is no clear guideline on choosing among them, and integer conversion and the zero-cell problem are the outstanding issues.literature: IPF/IPU/combinatorial optimisation/Markov the established families; no consensus on choice; integer conversion and zero cells the open problemsActivitySim ships PopulationSim; MATSim scenarios use eqasim's synthesiser or a bespoke one; every platform in the survey treats the synthetic population as an input rather than a modelled object.INsrc/build/build_population.py produces demand/population/B1_synthetic_population.csv seeded at B.seed.master = 20260810; B.population.build_sample_share = 1.0; the househThe population is the denominator of every share on the board. It is deterministic and hashed into the manifest, so it is one of the few layers a deviation cannot be blamed on without evidence.
Travel survey (HTS) weighting and vintageHousehold travel survey estimates are produced on a rolling basis from multiple pooled years and weighted to the ABS Estimated Resident Population for the collection year - so an HTS figure is a multi-year average, not a single-year observation. The survey's known systematic weakness is the undercount of short walk trips: every national survey from 1977 to 2022 has undercounted total walk trips by omitting short walks to stops and car parks.literature: HTS estimates are rolling multi-year pooled and ERP-weighted; walk trips systematically undercounted in every survey series examinedEvery activity-based model in the field calibrates against an HTS of this kind; the vintage-versus-base-year mismatch is universal and rarely stated.PARTIALNSW HTS is AGGREGATE-ONLY: src/analyse/measure_demographic_modes.py:15 records that hts_mode.csv and hts_purpose.csv "carry NO demographic column", and src/analyse/extracThis is the binding constraint behind half this ledger. Age, sex, income and purpose cannot be estimated because there are no unit records, so every segmentation gap - walk +64.7%, bike +198.4%, taxi +105.6% - is a data access problem before it is a modelling
Smartcard (Opal) and station countsSmartcard data is the standard calibration source for transit and it supports high-quality validation - agent-based models calibrated on it reach R-squared around 0.85 on on-board bus volumes - but it is structurally incomplete: most datasets capture only entry and egress points with no routing information, so trip-chaining is required to infer alighting stops and identify transfers.literature: smartcard-calibrated transit ABMs reach R^2 ~0.85 on on-board volumes; alighting and transfers must be inferred by trip-chainingVisum, Emme and MATSim scenarios all calibrate PT to smartcard boardings where available; per-station validation for every mode is uncommon.PARTIALThe published Opal FARE schedule is fully wired (DECISIONS 9.135, issue #98) and rail and tram targets come from disclosed boardings (DECISIONS 9.130), read station by stheavy_rail +417.1% is measured in boardings per weekday, and whether an Opal record is a journey or a tap decides the denominator of that comparison. An unobtained journey-linking rule is a live risk to the largest deviation on the board.
Road countsTraffic counts are not a fixed truth: counts alone vary by 10% or more from daily and seasonal variation, and FHWA recommends a minimum of one midweek 24-hour count at least every two years to obtain a typical ADT estimate. Validation percentages are therefore reported by functional class and against screenlines rather than link by link.literature: >=10% intrinsic variability in count data; validation reported by functional class and screenline, not per linkEvery four-step and ABM practice validates on counts; MATSim scenarios in the literature report link-count scatter as the primary validation.PARTIALCount stations are mapped to links by src/analyse/map_count_stations.py:58 under B.counts.station_match_radius_m, and B.counts.heavy_vehicle_share is declared; but CAL.obTruck sits at 7.35 against 15.47 on a network-wide road-vehicle basis and car at -13.0%; link counts are the observation that would separate "too few car trips" from "car trips on the wrong links". The stations are already mapped - only the objective and the l
GTFS and OSM completenessOpenStreetMap road completeness is about 83% globally (Barrington-Leigh and Millard-Ball 2017) and highest in cities; a 41,000 km Australian road network study finds OSM navigation performance correlates strongly with data quality, which itself tracks city population and ICT infrastructure. GTFS is the interoperable timetable format because timetables change too often for OSM; the join between the two (pt2matsim here) is the recurring failure point.literature: OSM roads ~83% complete globally, higher in cities; Australian OSM quality tracks population and ICTpt2matsim, OpenTripPlanner and UrbanAccess join GTFS to OSM; validators (gtfs-validator) check feed integrity but not map completeness.INThe network was rebuilt 16 August on the boundary-derived extent with 15 feeds mapped and 0 unmapped stops (STATUS P2); A.osm.harvest_margin_m and A.osm.buildings_margin_Supply completeness is ruled out as a cause of the PT deviations: bus +106.9%, light_rail -30.0% and heavy_rail +417.1% all run on a fully mapped schedule. That is a useful elimination for the report.

K. Computation — 3 factors

factorwhat the research saysmagnitudehow the leading simulators do itstatus hereproof at HEADwhat it would move
Sample fraction and scaling rulesDownscaling has measured limits: simulations at 25% or higher of the traveller population preserve all major urban traffic statistics, while below 10% even average statistics become unreliable, with scores and travel times the first to degrade. The scaling rule is that flowCapacityFactor follows the sample share and storageCapacityFactor is set a little higher at samples of 10% or below; in one published scenario a 1% population needed a 2% flow capacity factor to reproduce the observed travel-distance distributionliterature: >=25% preserves all major traffic statistics; below 10% even averages are unreliable; storage capacity factor set above flow at small samplesMATSim, SUMO and BEAM all scale link capacities with the sample; the field's usual practice is 1-10%, and 25% is at the high end of published scenarios.INRUN.sample.fraction with flowCapacityFactor = fraction (src/build/build_matsim_run_inputs.py:1280), RUN.sample.storage_capacity_exponent (src/run/run_matsim.py:394-400) aThe whole board is read at 25% under a standing 25%-only directive, and rail and tram are reported as boardings x1/fraction. heavy_rail's +417.1% is therefore a scaled number, and the scaling rule is the thing that has to be right for it to mean anything.
Iteration count and costThere is no standard iteration count: the process is run until the average population score stabilises, simple car-only scenarios converge fast, complex multimodal ones sometimes do not converge by iteration 100, one published scenario converged at iteration 164 and others run 500; because the simulation is stochastic, deterministic convergence criteria do not apply.literature: 100-500 iterations in published scenarios; one converged at 164; no multimodal twelve-mode benchmarkPublished MATSim scenarios commonly run 100-500 iterations with an innovation-off tail; eqasim and BEAM likewise.PARTIALRUN.controler.last_iteration is still 1000 and was deliberately NOT re-declared to 250 because DECISIONS 9.7 measured 250 insufficient; src/analyse/arm_cost.py:182-185 noThis is why the board is read at iteration 20 and why "Inside 10%: none" is not yet a finding about the model. GOAL.md requires convergence in at most 250 iterations and that requirement is UNMEASURED. Every ranked mover below is worth less than the arm that w
Reproducibility of a runRun-to-run reproducibility is not achievable by fixing a seed alone in this class of model: across 100 seeds relative errors up to 10% occur on high-volume links, and between-seed variation dominates the last-two-iteration within-seed variation. Reporting a single seeded run is therefore reporting one draw from a distribution.literature: up to 10% relative link-volume error across seeds; between-seed variation dominates within-seedAimsun and Vissim require multiple replications; most published MATSim scenarios report one seed and do not state the noise floor.PARTIALThe build side is fully deterministic and hashed (B.seed.master = 20260810, MANIFEST.csv over 512 files); the RUN side is not - DECISIONS 3.5 records ~18% of pt2matsim roIt forbids comparing any two readings from different builds, which is why every family boundary invalidates the arm before it. Combined with the unmeasured seed variance, it means no deviation on the board carries a confidence interval.

The failing gate, exactly

One run directory is missing from the board and from results/INDEX.csv: aborted_20260907T215740_4it_25pct, a four-iteration 25% probe launched at 21:57:40 — nine minutes after HEAD's commit — and stopped at 22:28. It carries a complete record with a quoted cause ("the session was reset to the merged PR #156… nothing it produced is wanted"), so the machinery worked. The board is simply one run behind. The staleness is not in the committed tree — results/ is gitignored and a fresh clone reproduces neither side — but it is load-bearing: gate-pr-on-docs.sh:42 runs the board check and fails closed, so the next session cannot open a pull request from this checkout until build_status_board.py and build_run_index.py are re-run.

Three control questions

Permissions

test.yml has no permissions: key at all — nine jobs run on the repository-default token, four of them pip install-ing unpinned packages. pages.yml:23-26 grants pages:write and id-token:write at workflow level, so the build job holds OIDC minting it never uses.

Pinning

Only the JDK and Maven are hash-pinned. pt2matsim (bootstrap_toolchain.py:142, downloaded with no expect) and the 201-jar run stack are trust-on-first-use; .tools/toolchain.json is gitignored; GitHub Actions sit on mutable major tags; and there is no requirements file at all — in a project whose own rule says a toolchain change is a model change.

Licence boundary

Visible in the manifest (512 rows, 0 blank licences) and stated in all three prose homes — but not at four crossings: 30 pt2matsim-mapped schedules and 10 OSM-derived parking-price files under scenarios/matsim/ are labelled CC-BY while identical content under networks/matsim/ is ODbL. build_manifest.py:282 already computes the raw ancestry that would settle it, and licence_for():362 never consults it.

The field and the factors

  • Appeared in the survey: SEMCOG ActivitySim activity-based model (Southeast Michigan / Detroit) - survey shares + road link counts, Washington DC metro MATSim model from open data, COVID case study (Ruan, Khan, Xin, Zufle, Pfoser; Computational Urban Science 5:57, 2025) - road link counts.
  • Moved rung: POLARIS Chicago now carries a 2026 sentence naming transit boardings, mode shares, departure-time and trip-length profiles (still no figure) — and our own row moved down, from one mode inside 10% to none.
  • Factor statuses that changed: route choice PARTIAL → IN on RUN.travel_time.filter_modes; reliability and headway newly proven INERT; mobility impairment newly proven INERT; constraints at both ends → IN; schedule delay → PARTIAL with a new finding — late_arrival_utils_per_h = −18.0 is emitted, but no activity carries an openingTime or latestStartTime, so the term can never bind.
  • The library paid for itself: not one stored row was re-searched in either lane. 56 searches were spent across both phases, all of them on the library's own recorded gaps, and both lanes stopped on the two-empty-rounds rule rather than on the budget.
Phase 8 · what to do next

Eighteen recommendations, ranked by what they prevent divided by what they cost

The first four cost nothing and change no output. Everything under opens a family makes the next arm incomparable with the last, so those are batched into one family boundary or not taken at all — and the last one is the only item on this list that answers a hard requirement.

How this report was produced, and how to reproduce it

Reproduce it

git checkout f40d332
python src/run/session_gate.py
python .claude/skills/project-report/scripts/collect_metrics.py      <scratch>
python .claude/skills/project-report/scripts/collect_code_metrics.py <scratch>
python .claude/skills/project-report/scripts/collect_performance.py  <scratch>

Then the six phase passes, one agent each, reading the collector output and the standing library at docs/reports/reference/. The embedded report-data block at the end of this file is what the next report diffs against.

The standing reference library

The dated reports in docs/reports/ are prunable files; the library is not. It holds the external half of the research — what the world outside this repository is and what the literature says — and deliberately holds no fact about this model, because a comparable project's engine does not change week to week while this model's coverage of a factor does.

filerowsthis pass
field-survey.json46 projects · 12 platforms · 53 excluded · 37 not re-verified · 4 gaps43 reused unchanged, 1 updated, 2 added, 0 re-searched; 1 gap closed (MATSim's licence — GNU GPL, per its own pom.xml), 1 added
factors.json72 factors · 2 still needing research69 literature halves reused unchanged, 3 completed; 0 statuses stored — all 72 were re-read at HEAD by grep, because a status carried forward is a status that is wrong

Sources

Every survey row carries at least one source URL and the date it was last verified. A row inside its horizon is rendered reused and was not fetched again this pass; a row searched and not re-found keeps its stored attributes and gains not_reverified_on — it is never emptied. Paywalled sources give unknown and say so. No literature value in this report is presented as an observation, and no coefficient in it was invented.
